column1: # M1: MCP gateway, chrome-devtools pair (see ~/dotfiles/CLAUDE.md, "MCP gateway")

column9: Service state, health endpoint, served servers (desktop-ro, telegram, chrome-devtools, chrome-devtools-mine, context7) and the token file mode. The gateway is a user service on 127.0.0.1:37411.

column6: mcp-gateway restart && notify-send -a mcp 'MCP gateway restarted'
column9: Restarts mcp-gateway.service (re-reads the servers, e.g. after the Telegram setup).

column3: MCP: register servers in Claude Code and Codex
column9: Registers every gateway server in Claude Code (user scope) and Codex with a token-less headers helper, and removes the old mcphub and direct chrome-devtools entries. Safe to rerun. Backups of ~/.codex/config.toml are written first.
column10: x a;Register servers in the CLIs

column3: MCP: install or update the pinned servers
column9: mcp-proxy, the desktop-ro venv and chrome-devtools-mcp, from the pins in ~/.config/mcp (hash-checked, no root).

ON = the gateway server chrome-devtools-mine attaches to YOUR logged-in Chrome (it switches itself off after 60 minutes). Chrome still asks you to allow the connection at chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging. OFF = agents only get the clean automation Chromium (chrome-devtools).

column3: Telegram MCP: set up or re-login (QR)
column9: One-time (and after a terminated session): QR login, tick the chats the AI may read, seal the credentials with the TPM2 (sudo password), start the read-only service. The session string is stored in Bitwarden (MCP/telegram-mcp, field session).

column3: Telegram MCP: choose the readable chats
column9: Extend or shrink the chat allowlist (Tab on an [allowed] chat removes it). Uses the session stored in Bitwarden.
telegram-mcp.service, the on-demand whisper socket and whether the gateway serves telegram.

Collects the focused window's class, title and geometry plus a screenshot of that window only (not for password managers or while locked) and opens a Claude session about it. Nothing is sent anywhere by the AI; it only drafts.

column3: Ask about the focused window (text only, no screenshot)
column9: Same as the window hotkey but without the screenshot.
Takes the primary selection (else the clipboard text, never a sensitive entry), asks your question (Enter = explain it) and opens the answer in a Claude session.

A Claude session with only the read-only telegram MCP server summarises the unread messages of the allowlisted chats by urgency (voice messages are transcribed locally). It never sends: drafts are shown and copied to the clipboard on request. Needs mcp-telegram-setup.
